thread:
sam: ran a perf sweep this morning comparing Mixtral-8B served as draft vs Qwen-7B as speculative fallback. saw weird KV cache churn when tokenizers/rope configs differ. attaching short profile.
anya: ping, can you paste the flame or a short log? :eyes:
sam: main symptom: tail latency spikes on long contexts (>2k). throughput ok. logs show repeated KV invalidations and re-allocs.
sam: snippet from the short profiler:
```
KVCache: alloc 98% on seq>2048
KernelSwitch: frequent (bert-attn -> rope-compat)
SpecDecode: accept_rate drop from 0.78 -> 0.41 when using Qwen drafts
Batching: avg batch size 6 -> 3 under the same qps
```
javier: interesting — is this only on Mixtral->Qwen pairing or also Mixtral->Mistral? any tokenizer mismatch warnings?
sam: mostly Mixtral draft + Qwen speculative. Mistral pairing behaves better. Tokenizer vocab overlap is ~92% but encoding choices differ for long numeric-chunk sequences.
liz: could RoPE scaling mismatch be causing cache misses? if head dims or rope base differs we might be invalidating cached kvs.
hao: yeah, RoPE scale mismatch can change positional embeddings, we tag cached KV entries by model family + rope_scale in runtime. maybe the tag resolution logic is too coarse and we end up evicting when model variants considered compatible.
anya: do we have kernel selection traces? maybe runtime is swapping to a safer kernel when it detects mismatched heads.
sam: kernel trace shows fallback to generic attention kernel ~15% of calls during the spike window. looks like the kernel selector sees differing head counts (mixtral 32 vs qwen 40) and chooses a compatibility kernel that is slower and not kv-cache-friendly.
javier: that explains latency. Any ideas on acceptance-rate tuning? speculative decoding acceptance threshold currently 0.6 for family mismatch.
liz: lowering acceptance threshold reduces acceptance (ha) no, increases acceptance? wait — lowering threshold makes speculative outputs more likely to be accepted, which cuts latency but risks quality regressions.
hao: suggested experiment: run acceptance=0.5 and keep rope_scale strict tag so we avoid cache eviction. compare token cost and top-k disagree rate.
sam: ran a quick A/B: acceptance=0.5 with strict rope tags -> tail p99 latency down 120ms, but spec accept_rate down 0.35 for the problematic prompts (numeric-chunk). quality delta small on BLEU-like metric used for eval.
anya: can we do a middle ground: allow tokenizer-alias mapping (map special numeric tokens) + kernel hint so selector picks optimized kernel despite head mismatch?
ajavier: grammar nit: javier's name, but ok
javier: yes — runtime could accept a kernel-hint header from model pairings where we've previously validated shape-compat. then we only use compatibility kernel when shape mismatch unavoidable.
liz: ops question: how expensive is re-tagging kv entries by rope_scale? could do fine-grained tags including head_count+kv_dim+rope_scale.
hao: re-tagging at entry time is cheap, but lookup cost rises slightly. main cost today is allocation churn when we evict large KV shards; avoiding eviction is big win.
sam: proposed short action items:
- add kernel_hint metadata to model-pairing table (sam)
- make kv tag include head_count and rope_scale (hao)
- run AB with acceptance thresholds 0.5 vs 0.6 and strict tagging (anya + perf-bot)
- add tokenizer alias mapping for numeric sequences (javier)
anya: I'll schedule the perf run — perf-bot will post results.
perf-bot: scheduled perf job 2026-04-02T10:00Z -> job id pb-7789
liz: one more thought — for batching heuristics: if speculative fallback frequently reduces batch size, consider a speculative-aware batching window (hold short 10ms) to let speculative acceptances coalesce.
sam: good call. adding a 10ms speculative buffer as a toggle in runtime.
javier: ok, I'll start the tokenizer mapping patch today. tagging for review @sam @hao.
sam: thanks everyone. let's reconvene after pb-7789 completes. :thumbsup:
